html:
Sadriddin Ayni was a writer and scholar, the founder of modern Tajik literature. He was born in 1878 in a village near Bukhara and trained in its madrasas.

As a young man he joined the Jadid reformers who wanted new schools, and the emir had him flogged in 1917. He sided with the Soviets after the revolution. When the new borders of the 1920s gave Samarkand and Bukhara to Uzbekistan, he wrote an anthology of Tajik poetry to prove that Tajiks were a nation with a past of their own, from Rudaki onward.

His novels and his memoirs of old Bukhara set the style of modern Tajik prose. He became the first president of the Tajik Academy of Sciences in 1951. He died in Dushanbe in 1954, and a square, a theatre and a district there carry his name.
sum: Sadriddin Ayni was a writer and scholar, the founder of modern Tajik literature. He was born in 1878 in a village near Bukhara and trained in its madrasas.
